summary: Anthropic Claude Chat Models integration — Backend 100% PASS (6/6 pytest), Frontend model picker & per-message model send-and-receive works with real Claude Sonnet 4.6 & Haiku 4.5 responses, but the ASSISTANT MESSAGE HEADER does NOT render the model label — it only shows 'NOVA' instead of the spec-required 'NOVA · CLAUDE SONNET 4.6'. The `data-testid=chat-message-model-{i}` element is not implemented in the source. `modelLabel` is stored in state and returned by backend but never rendered in the header. All other acceptance criteria met.

ui_bugs.issue: Spec requires assistant message header to render 'NOVA · <MODEL_LABEL>' (e.g. 'NOVA · CLAUDE SONNET 4.6') and expose a data-testid `chat-message-model-{i}`. Actual header renders only the static string 'Nova' (uppercased via textTransform). The `msg.modelLabel` value IS correctly plumbed through (state line 22, populated on send response line 267, hydrated from history line 182) but never rendered into a <Text> element. So users cannot see which model produced each message, and automation cannot select by the required testid.

critical_code_review_comments: personal_assistant.py: DEFAULT_CHAT_MODEL fallback (line 419-421) is a good silent-fallback pattern. Consider logging a warning when an unknown model key is submitted so misconfiguration is visible in observability.

personal_assistant.py DELETE /sessions/{id} (line 507) targets `db.assistant_sessions` and `db.assistant_messages` collections, but every other endpoint in the file writes to `db.personal_assistant_sessions` and `db.personal_assistant_messages`. This DELETE endpoint is a dead-op (always returns 404 or silently deletes 0 messages). Not related to Claude integration but worth fixing.

AIChatPanel.tsx: the ChatMessage interface already carries `modelLabel` and is populated from backend, but the render layer drops it entirely. Storing without displaying is worse than not storing — please wire the header render as the ONE-liner fix above.

CHAT_MODELS dict is fine as an in-file dict but as the model catalog grows, consider extracting to a small yaml/json config plus a Pydantic validator so a new model is one config change with no code diff.

personal_assistant.py line 466 uses `.with_model(model_cfg['provider'], model_cfg['model'])` — good. Consider passing max_tokens / temperature per model config to give the picker more meaningful control.

missing_model_label_in_assistant_header.reproduction: 1) Login as free user 2) goto /features/ai-writer 3) click AI Chat tab 4) select 'Claude Sonnet 4.6' pill 5) send any short message 6) wait for response 7) inspect the assistant bubble header — it says only 'NOVA' with no model suffix; querySelectorAll('[data-testid^="chat-message-model-"]').length === 0.
missing_model_label_in_assistant_header.root_cause: In /app/frontend/src/components/AIChatPanel.tsx around line 610, the assistant header renders <Text>Nova</Text> as a static string. The message state carries `modelLabel` (interface line 22, hydrated on send line 267, from history line 182), but it is never composed into the header text nor exposed with the required data-testid `chat-message-model-{i}`. Backend correctly returns model_label — the entire gap is one line of React Native/Web JSX.
missing_model_label_in_assistant_header.mitigation: Replace the static Nova header <Text> with: <Text data-testid={`chat-message-model-${i}`} testID={`chat-message-model-${i}`} style={...unchanged...}>{msg.modelLabel ? `Nova · ${msg.modelLabel}` : 'Nova'}</Text>. Then rebuild the Expo web export. Consider uppercasing consistently (already textTransform: 'uppercase' inline). No backend changes needed.
